text: Pulled the splits from the last five editions. The winning time has moved by 40 seconds total in ten years, but the 100th-place time is four minutes faster. The depth changed, the front didn't.
label: analysis

text: I tracked sleep against session quality for eleven weeks. Under seven hours the next day's intervals were 6-8 seconds per mile slower, every time bar one. Small sample, one runner, but it's consistent enough that I've stopped scheduling hard days after late shifts.
label: analysis

text: The club championship scoring changed in 2019 from top-6 to top-10. Since then our B team has finished above the A team twice. That's not depth improving, it's the scoring rewarding turnout.
label: hot_take

text: Everyone blames the hill at 18 miles. I split the field into people who ran the first half under 1:45 and over, and the slowdown after 18 was almost identical for both groups. If the hill were the problem the fast starters would fall apart harder.
label: hot_take

text: Carbon plates aren't the whole story. My times dropped 2% in the shoes and another 2% the following year in the same pair, when the only thing that changed was going from 35 to 50 miles a week.
label: analysis

text: Checked the entry lists. 41% of this year's field have never run the distance before, against 26% five years ago. That's why the finish-line photos look different, not because standards dropped.
label: analysis

text: Ran the same loop in 4C and in 24C within a fortnight, same effort by heart rate. 90 seconds slower in the heat over six miles. People keep saying heat costs you 'a bit' and it's more than that.
label: hot_take

text: Went back through the club results going back to 2012. Every single year the number of people who enter the spring marathon and don't start it sits between 18 and 23 percent. It's not a bad-luck year, it's the base rate.
label: analysis

text: The 10K route was remeasured in 2021 and came out 60 metres long. Everyone comparing PBs from before and after that is comparing two different races, which is about 12 seconds at club pace.
label: analysis

text: Three of us ran the same session on the same day, different shoes, within 10 seconds of each other over 5 miles. I'm not saying shoes do nothing, but whatever they do was smaller than the noise between three people.
label: reaction

text: Anyone who races more than once a month isn't training, they're just collecting medals.
label: hot_take

text: Heart rate zones are astrology for runners.
label: hot_take

text: The club needs to stop pretending the Tuesday session is for everyone. It isn't and it never has been.
